sentences.text:
"MEMORANDUM OF SETTLEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF CPC READ WITH RULES 24 AND 25 OF THE KARNATAKA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION) RULES, 2005.
I.
The Petitioner has filed this petition against the Respondent under Section 13 (1) (i-a) (iii) of the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 for dissolution of her marriage with the respondent.
II. The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the dispute between the parties.

During the course of mediation, the parties have resolved their dispute and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:
1. The petitioner and the respondent are Hindus by religion.

Their marriage was solemnized on 26.12.2021 at Shri Krishna Dhama Sabha Bhavana, Saraswathipuram,
Mysore, as per Hindu rites and customs.

Subsequently their marriage was registered before the Registrar of Marriage, Mysore vide certificate No. MYS-HM1268-2021- 22 dated 31.12.2021 and stored in C. D. No. MYSM40,
2.
The parties state and admit that due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, they are living separately from 16.03.2023.
The efforts made by the elders, friends and well wishers to resolve the differences between the parties did not yield any fruits.
There is absolutely no chance of a reunion between the NC: 2024:KHC:44686 parties.
Hence, the petitioner and the respondent have decided to get the marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce.
3. Both the parties state that they have no children born to them from their wedlock.
4. The petitioner has agreed to pay Rs.10,20,000/- (Rupees Ten lakhs twenty thousand only) to the respondent towards all her claims of maintenance/permanent alimony.
The said amount is transferred to her account by way of RTGS.
The respondent/wife acknowledges the receipt of the said amount.
5. The parties herein state that they have no claims over movable, immovable belonging to each other either at present or to be acquired or inherited in a later stage.
6. The parties admit and agree that they have no further claims of whatsoever manner against each other either past, present or future.
7. Both the parties have agreed that they have exchanged their gold and valuable items.
8. The respondent/wife had filed a complaint bearing Crime No 170/2022 before the HAL Police station.
In view of the settlement she has agreed to withdraw the same.
9. The parties admit and agree that there is no collusion or force, fraud or any undue influence in filing the above petition and entering into this compromise in the aforesaid manner.

D. No. MYSM40. by granting a decree of divorce in terms of this agreement.
12. Parties will appear on 18.12.2023 before the Hon'ble Court for passing of orders in terms of the agreement."

4. In the light of application compounding for being filed along with the memorandum of settlement and offences not being against the State, I deem it appropriate to accept the same and terminate the proceedings against these petitioners in the subject petition.

5. Therefore, in the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties as afore-quoted, the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is disposed.
ii. Proceedings pending in C.C.No.54776/2024 pending before the 29th Additional CMM, Mayohall 10, Bengaluru City, stand quashed, qua the petitioners.
